examples.title: Context-Aware Rendering › With Field and Control Wrappers
examples.code:
function example() {
  return (
    <Field
      horizontal
      label="RSVP"
      labelProps={{ id: 'rsvp-label-control', htmlFor: undefined }}
    >
      <Field.Body>
        <Field>
          <Control>
            <Radios aria-labelledby="rsvp-label-control">
              <Radio name="rsvp3"> Attend </Radio>
              <Radio name="rsvp3"> Decline </Radio>
              <Radio name="rsvp3"> Tentative </Radio>
            </Radios>
          </Control>
        </Field>
      </Field.Body>
    </Field>
  );
}

accessibility:
- By default the group is rendered as a `<div class="radios" role="radiogroup">` containing labeled radio buttons.
- The `label` prop names the whole group: the rendered `<label>` gets an id (yours via `labelProps.id`, or a generated one) and the group points at it with `aria-labelledby`.
- Inside a labeled `Field`, that `Field`'s label names the group the same way.
- With `as="fieldset"`, the group is a native `<fieldset>` with `role="radiogroup"`, named by its `<legend>` where it renders its own `Field`, or by an outer `Field`'s label through `aria-labelledby` inside one.
- An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` you give the group wins over either label, whether that label sits on the Radios or on a `Field` around them.
- Each child should be a `Radio` for proper labeling and accessibility.
- Use the same `name` for all radios in a group to ensure mutual exclusivity.
summary: The `Radios` component wraps multiple `Radio` components in a Bulma-styled group.

parts.summary: The `Radios` component wraps multiple `Radio` components in a Bulma-styled group.

props.name: label
props.description: Field label naming the whole group. Automatically associated via `aria-labelledby` on the `role="radiogroup"` wrapper — uses your `labelProps.id` when provided, otherwise a generated one. Dropped inside an outer `Field`, whose own label names the group instead through `aria-labelledby` when that `Field` generates a target id (not `grouped`/`hasAddons`, no explicit `labelProps.htmlFor`). An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` you set on the group wins over either label, which still renders but no longer names it. An `aria-labelledby` key counts even when undefined, since it is spread over the group's own.

props.name: labelProps
props.description: Props for the label element. An explicit `id` here is used as the `aria-labelledby` target instead of a generated one; any `htmlFor` is ignored (a group label names the group, never a single control).

props.name: name
props.description: Form field name shared by every Radio in the group (via context).

props.name: children
props.description: Radio elements to render in the group.

props.name: as
props.description: The element the group renders as. With `fieldset` it's a native `<fieldset>` that keeps `role="radiogroup"`. Where the group renders a `Field` of its own, that `Field` is the `<fieldset>` and the `label` is its `<legend>`, in the label column when `horizontal`, so the legend names the group with no ids to wire. Your other attributes then go on the `<fieldset>`, while `className` and the helper props stay on the box that lays out the radios. Inside an outer `Field` there's no legend: the group element itself is the `<fieldset>`, named by that `Field`'s label as before. `div`, the default, renders the group as it always has.

props.name: labelSize
props.description: Size for the label (used in horizontal layouts).

props.name: fieldClassName
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the Field wrapper.

parts.summary: The `Radio` component provides a Bulma-styled radio button input with flexible labels and helper classes.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes, on the outer `<label>`. That's the element that declares the `--bulma-radio-*` variables, so a class is how to set one: `style` and the other input attributes go to the `<input>`. Name `.styled-radio` beside your class in the selector, so it beats the label's own declaration whatever order the stylesheets load in. A `color` prop declares the active color again on `.styled-radio.is-<color>`, which ties that selector, so leave `color` unset when a class sets it.

parts.catchAll: All standard <input> attributes and Bulma helper props
parts.helperPropsNote: Helper props go on the outer `<label>`, with `className`. The other attributes go on the `<input>`.
